title: A week of careful speech
hookLine: no gossip, no harsh words, for seven days
tomorrow: soldiers lead a man out. he stops to touch the doorpost. why?

lines: A SCREENSHOT AND A ROW OF LAUGHING FACES.
THE ANSWER IS ABOUT THE MOUTH.
cards: A group chat lights up with a screenshot and a row of crying-laughing faces. Nobody's lying. It's just about someone who isn't in the chat.
There's a rabbi who wrote a whole book about that moment, and he's known by its title, two words from a Psalm: Chafetz Chaim, desiring life.
The Psalm asks, "Who is the man that desireth life, and loveth days, that he may see good therein?" Its answer is about the mouth.

teach.b: Here's the next line: "Keep thy tongue from evil, and thy lips from speaking guile."

teach.h: LASHON HARA: EVEN WHEN IT'S TRUE.
teach.b: The book is about lashon hara, the evil tongue: saying something negative about a person who isn't there, even when it's true. True is the surprising part. Being accurate doesn't make it kind.
And notice where the Psalm files it: not under manners, under the question of life itself. Whoever wants good days starts with the tongue.
So a week of careful speech is easy to say and hard to keep: no gossip, no harsh words, for seven days, and a tally when you slip.
Now hold this week's rule up to the light. A coin in the pushke: a coin a week. Ten minutes on the calendar: fix a time.
Isaac in his field: the middle of the day. The merchant at the till: look back kindly.
Mar Zutra in bed: forgive before sleeping. The world's third pillar: one kindness a day. And now the mouth, the tool you carry everywhere.

how: Some Jews study a short daily portion of the Chafetz Chaim's laws of speech, and some schools and families take on 'speech weeks' or a set hour each day free of lashon hara.

games.q: what does “a week of careful speech” mean?
o: a week of silence, with no talking at all
seven days with no gossip and no harsh words
a week of saying only nice things online

p: harmful talk about someone, even if true

s: lashon hara only means spreading lies
it's negative talk about someone not there, even when it's true.
the rabbi known as the Chafetz Chaim is named for his book, from Psalm 34
'who is the man that desireth life': chafetz chaim.
a week of careful speech means not talking at all
no gossip, no harsh words; the rest of speech is open.

games.q: a friend tells you something true but embarrassing about a classmate. you checked: it's accurate. under a week of careful speech, can you pass it on?
o: yes; it's true, so it isn't gossip.
no; lashon hara is harmful talk about someone, even when it's true.
yes, as long as you add that you're not judging.
games.why: true is the surprising part: accuracy doesn't make it kind. the tally would count it.

practice: Hold up one hand, fingers open. Go back through today's conversations and fold one finger down for each time you said something about someone who wasn't there.
No verdicts, just the count; then open your hand again and rest it on your knee.

wordCard.voice: A week of careful speech: seven days with no lashon hara and no harsh words, kept with a simple tally.

orig.note: Hebrew: the evil tongue; harmful talk about a person, even if true.

carryVoice: Hold on to this one: seven days of clean speech. One hand, one tally, and nobody talked about who isn't there.
